subject.title: [Feature]: Disable image optimization when images are uploaded to Slack

question: Should Slack uploads preserve original media bytes by default, expose a default-off raw-upload or image-optimization opt-out, or keep the current optimizing media pipeline and document a different workflow?
rationale: This changes Slack media-delivery semantics and likely adds config/default behavior, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive rather than a safe autonomous bug fix.

options.title: Add Default-Off Fidelity Control
options.body: Add a Slack-owned opt-in that bypasses image optimization for explicit uploads while leaving existing default behavior and oversize fallback policy intact.

options.title: Make Raw Upload Default
options.body: Preserve original bytes by default for Slack uploads, accepting the upgrade risk that some previously optimized sends may fail or behave differently.

options.title: Keep Current Pipeline
options.body: Document that Slack uploads use the shared media pipeline and close or narrow the request if maintainers do not want a Slack fidelity contract.

recommendation.title: Add Default-Off Fidelity Control
recommendation.body: Add a Slack-owned opt-in that bypasses image optimization for explicit uploads while leaving existing default behavior and oversize fallback policy intact.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans shared media loading, Slack plugin delivery, and config compatibility, where the strongest current history points to steipete.
